issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class and attribute named 'Stock' (the UML shows class Stock and SealSaloon.stock of type Stock). However, the repository (both template and solution) provides a class named Inventory that implements the expected stock behavior and SealSaloon uses Inventory as the type of its static stock field. This divergent identifier naming (Stock vs Inventory) refers to the same conceptual entity and will confuse students: they will search for/expect a Stock class as described in the exercise but find Inventory instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the provided Inventory class (file and type) to Stock and update all references (SealSaloon, tests, and documentation) so the exercise text and code use 'Stock', and remove the empty Stock.java; or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and tests to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock' and remove or deprecate the empty Stock.java file. Ensure all example code and SealSaloon signatures use the same type name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require SealSaloon to have a static attribute 'stock' of type Stock. In the repository (solution and template usage), SealSaloon declares a static field named 'stock' of type Inventory (private static final Inventory stock = new Inventory()). In addition, Stock.java in the repository is an empty file. This mismatch between the expected attribute type (Stock) and the actual attribute type (Inventory), plus the empty Stock.java, creates a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which class to use/implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the type mismatch so the exercise text and code agree. Options: (A) Provide a concrete Stock class (matching the UML API) or rename Inventory to Stock so SealSaloon.stock can be declared as Stock; remove the empty Stock.java file. (B) Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to specify that SealSaloon.stock is of type Inventory and remove the empty Stock.java. Ensure the attribute in SealSaloon, example code, and tests all reference the same concrete type.
